name: confluence-extract-package
description: Use when the user asks to extract a Confluence package, download a Confluence page plus linked pages, build a package from Confluence page {ID}, or gather discovery input from Confluence. Given a Confluence page ID or URL, extracts the main page plus all linked pages and Jira issues (L0 only), checks for related Jira packages, performs staleness checks, and prints a Package Update Report.

name: confluence-fetch
description: Use when the user asks to fetch, view, cache, or analyze a single Confluence page by ID or URL; says 'fetch Confluence page', 'show me page {ID}', 'read this Confluence URL', or needs raw page JSON and metadata for agent analysis. Saves the raw JSON response and metadata, then lets the agent generate markdown analysis when needed.

name: create-design-package
description: Use when the user asks to create, build, write, or assemble a design package; says 'create the design package', 'design the solution', 'build the technical blueprint', 'create the architecture', 'how should we build this', 'start the design stage', 'choose the technology stack', 'design the API/database/frontend/backend'. Drives the full design stage: optional architecture-baseline discovery (brownfield), 11-step design assembly with C4 diagrams, technology pinning, traceability back to requirements — handing off to review-design-package.

name: review-design-package
description: Use when the user asks to review, validate, or check readiness of an assembled design package; says 'review the design package', 'review the solution design', 'validate the design', 'check design readiness', 'architecture review', 'security posture review', 'is the design ready for implementation', 'solution readiness', 'implementation handoff'. Independently invocable; assumes the design package is already assembled.

name: create-pr
description: Use when the user asks to create a PR, prepare a pull request, package the diff into commits, review the working-tree diff before committing, generate a PR description, or hand off implementation work for merge. Reviews uncommitted changes, creates atomic conventional commits, and produces a PR description with summary and test plan.

name: execute-increments
description: Use when the user asks to execute the implementation plan, run an increment, ship INC-XXX, work the next increment, run the AI gate, run the human gate, or turn an approved implementation package into working code. Executes one increment at a time with TDD, AI Gate, Human Gate, and increment-status updates.

name: manage-bugs
description: Use when the user asks to log a bug, capture an issue, review open bugs, triage bugs for the current increment, close a bug, or manage the bugs-and-issues log. Independently invocable: works whether or not an increment is being executed. Operates on bugs-and-issues-log.md in the implementation package.

name: document-convert
description: Use when the user asks to convert or analyze a Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx/.xls), or PDF (.pdf) document; says 'convert this document', 'analyze this spreadsheet', 'turn this PDF into markdown', or needs document content transformed into markdown with structured analysis. Auto-detects format, converts to markdown, analyzes content, and generates actionable structured reports rather than only raw tables.

name: jira-extract-requirements
description: Use when the user asks to extract requirements from Jira, create a requirements package from a Jira Feature/Epic, build requirements from Jira, or says 'extract requirements for {KEY}'. Fetches the Jira issue, detects issue type, prompts for output location, saves raw data to cache, creates a structured markdown requirements package, performs staleness checks, and prints a Package Update Report.

name: jira-get
description: Use when the user asks to fetch, view, cache, or analyze a single Jira issue by key; says 'fetch PROJ-123', 'show me Jira issue {KEY}', 'get this Jira ticket', or needs raw Jira issue JSON and metadata for agent analysis. Saves the raw JSON response, metadata, and agent-generated markdown analysis by default to cache/jira/{projectKey}/{ISSUE_KEY}/.

name: jira-search
description: Use when the user asks to search Jira issues, run a JQL query, find issues by status, assignee, project, sprint, labels, or custom criteria, or says 'show me all issues matching...'. Translates search intent into JQL where needed, returns multiple issues with summaries, and generates search reports.

name: build-knowledge-base
description: Use when initialising a project's knowledge base for the first time, scaffolding the KB after reverse-engineering Part A/B docs land, building the KB on a brownfield onboarding, populating an empty knowledge_base_path, or generating ARCHITECTURE.md plus components/ plus graph.json from RE outputs. Replaces the legacy build-knowledge-repository-phase aggregator.

name: build-mainframe-data-lineage
description: Use when the user asks to build mainframe data lineage, generate cross-program field-level traceability, build a where-used index for COBOL copybooks or fields, build the JCL → program → dataset chain, resolve EXEC SQL host variables back to copybook fields, or aggregate copybook + COBOL program + JCL Part A into a coherent lineage artefact in the knowledge base. Runs after reverse-engineer-copybook-library, reverse-engineer-cobol-program, and reverse-engineer-jcl-job have all completed Part A for the contributing repos.

name: detect-knowledge-base-drift
description: Use when source repos may have changed without the KB being updated, when running a PR-gate freshness check, or for the scheduled (cron / weekly) drift sweep. Performs cheap-to-expensive layered detection (commit-stamp / structural diff / LLM contradiction / coverage sweep) and reports drift with per-component severity and recommended actions.

name: navigate-knowledge-base
description: Use when any stage skill (requirements, design, planning, execution, quick-dev) needs to load grounding context from the KB before starting work, or when a feature description / change scope arrives and only a minimal component subset must be selected to read. Returns the ranked component file list for the agent to load — the agent must NOT read the whole KB.

name: update-knowledge-base
description: Use when a feature has just shipped and the KB must be brought back into sync — invoked as the closing step of execute-increments or execute-quick-change. Updates only the components matched by the diff, appends to change-tracker, emits an ADR if a threshold is crossed, and incrementally regenerates graph.json and the capability index. Never re-runs a full build.

name: verify-knowledge-base-coverage
description: Use when running the scheduled coverage sweep (baseline on first build, delta on subsequent runs), confirming every public artifact in source repos maps to ≥1 component, finding KB entries with no source backing, or validating the freshly built KB after build-knowledge-base ran. Emits orphan + stale + warning reports; never modifies the KB.

name: customize-framework
description: Use when the user says "customize the framework", "override a skill", "change a skill default", "suppress this artifact", "pin this elicitation answer", "make this project-specific", "author a customization", or anytime they want to change behavior without editing the framework's shipped files. Walks the user through writing overrides under the right config layer (framework.user.toml, project.toml, project.user.toml, customizations/{skill}.toml or .user.toml) without hand-TOML editing. Covers scalar override, table merge, array-of-tables merge by code/id, and the _suppress: true marker.

name: framework-navigator
description: Use when the user asks for help choosing or finding a skill, says 'help', 'what's next', 'what should I do next', 'what's my best option', 'how do I…', 'where do I start', 'I'm not sure which skill', 'what skills are available', 'show me the catalog', 'list all the skills', or describes a goal in plain English instead of invoking a specific skill (e.g. 'I want a quick change to this project', 'I want to RE this API into the global KB', 'help me write requirements'). Routes to the right skill based on workspace state and goal description; supports goal mode (state probe + match + recommend) and catalog mode (stage-grouped listing). Reads project.toml and on-disk artifacts, then names exactly one downstream skill and the trigger phrase to invoke it. Never performs the work itself.

name: scaffold-documentation
description: Use when the user says "scaffold the docs", "set up the doc structure", "propose the file structure", "create the documentation skeleton", or after completing an inventory/discovery phase and needing to organize findings into a file structure before extraction or authoring begins. Cross-stage utility — works for RE, requirements, design, and KB packages. Enforces the "structure before content" principle.

name: shard-document
description: Use when a markdown document has grown too large to navigate (architecture doc, big requirements package, monolithic design file) or when the user says "shard this doc", "split this markdown", "break this file into sections". Splits a single .md at H2 boundaries into a folder of smaller files and resolves what to do with the original.

name: start-project
description: Use when the user says "start a new project", "set up A.I.D.E.", "bootstrap the project", "initialize the framework", "start the framework", "begin a new product", "begin a brownfield analysis", "start a quick fix", or whenever the user is invoking A.I.D.E. for the first time on a repository (or wants to re-bootstrap an existing one). Single entry point that elicits flow choice, captures project super-context, writes project.toml (and optionally project.user.toml), and hands off to the first skill of the chosen flow.

name: track-change
description: Use when the user says "log a change", "update the change tracker", "record this update", "track this edit", "add to the change log", or after finishing any documentation, requirements, design, or code change that touches a tracked package. Logs the change in a standardized CHANGE-TRACKER.md with Parts Affected, source version, and verification status.

name: verify-source
description: Use when the user says "verify the docs", "check this against source", "are these claims source-verified", "audit the package", "validate the spec", or after assembling any requirements / design / RE / KB package and before declaring it done. Generic content-vs-source verifier — runs completeness, accuracy, consistency, and change-tracking checks against the cited source artifacts (code, tickets, prior packages) for any package type.

name: create-implementation-package
description: Use when the user asks to create an implementation plan, set up coding increments, build the implementation package, decompose a design into INC-XXX increments, start the planning stage, or break a solution design into independently executable units. Produces an implementation package whose increments conform to the Canonical Increment Shape.

name: review-implementation-package
description: Use when the user asks to review the implementation package, validate the implementation plan before coding starts, run the pre-execution gate, check increment readiness, verify increments conform to the Canonical Increment Shape, or confirm INC-XXX coverage. Produces a GO/NO-GO verdict with per-increment findings.

name: audit-quality-coverage
description: Use when the user asks to audit test coverage against an implementation package, check whether all increments have test coverage, produce a coverage report, find INCs with no tests, detect coverage drift, or run a pre-release coverage check; says 'check quality coverage', 'audit coverage', 'are all increments covered', 'coverage report', 'which INCs have no tests', 'coverage gap', 'pre-release quality audit'. Independently invocable at any time; read-only against source code; creates the test-case status tracker only if missing.

name: create-quality-package
description: Use when the user asks to create, build, write, or assemble a quality package; says 'create the quality package', 'plan the testing', 'write the test strategy', 'design the tests', 'how will we test this', 'set up the quality plan', 'start the quality stage', 'define quality gates', 'plan test automation', or 'create the QA plan'. Drives the full quality stage: quality strategy (QA analysis), test design traced to acceptance criteria, and a quality-engineering plan (automation, CI gates, test data) — handing off to review-quality-package.

name: execute-quality-increments
description: Use when the user asks to execute quality / test-case increments, implement TC-XXX, build the test artifacts, run the next quality increment, or turn an approved quality package into working test code. Executes one test-case increment at a time, producing the actual test artifacts (feature files, step definitions, runners, fixtures, exports) and updating the test-case-status tracker. Optional path after a GO quality package when the team has opted into the TC-XXX increment flow.

name: review-quality-package
description: Use when the user asks to review, validate, or check readiness of an assembled quality package; says 'review the quality package', 'validate the test plan', 'check test coverage', 'is the quality plan ready', 'quality gate review', 'check the test strategy', 'review the test design', 'are the quality gates measurable', or 'quality readiness for execution'. Independently invocable; assumes the quality package is already assembled.

name: review-test-failures
description: Use when the user asks to review test failures, analyse why tests failed, triage failed scenarios, walk through defects, or determine root cause of a failing run; says 'my tests failed', 'analyse the failures', 'review the failures', 'what went wrong', 'triage the failed scenarios', or after execute-quality-increments / execute-increments / a CI run hands off with failure details. Walks through each failure one at a time, classifies as script issue / application defect / environment-or-data / flaky, proposes a remediation routed to a named framework skill, and waits for explicit user approval before advancing. Outputs a structured summary with action items grouped by routing target.

name: document-quick-change
description: Use when the user says "quick change", "small change", "fast-track this", "expedited spec", "write a change spec", or "document a small fix/feature" and the change does not warrant a full requirements + design package. Captures one combined lightweight spec (mini-requirements + mini-design in a single artifact) per `templates/compositions/quick-dev-spec.yaml`. First of three quick-dev skills.

name: execute-quick-change
description: Use when a quick-dev plan exists and the user says "execute the quick change", "implement the quick plan", "run the increments", or "do the work and PR it". Implements each increment with TDD and 3-dimension verification, runs adversarial PR review, creates atomic commits, and closes by handing off to `update-knowledge-base --scope=catalog-only`. Third of three quick-dev skills.

name: plan-quick-change
description: Use when a quick-dev spec has been agreed and the user says "plan this", "create the quick plan", "plan the quick change", "break this into increments", or wants to set up the lightweight implementation plan before coding. Authors a small set of increments (typically 1–3) using a reduced increment shape and runs a clarity gate before execution. Second of three quick-dev skills.

name: create-requirements-package
description: Use when the user asks to create, gather, build, write, or assemble a requirements package; says 'create requirements', 'gather requirements', 'document business requirements', 'start the requirements stage', 'write functional requirements', 'build the requirements package', or wants to begin a new feature/project from a clean slate. Drives the full requirements stage end-to-end: discovery (brownfield), analysis, writing, and assembly into the requirements package — handing off to review-requirements-package.

name: review-requirements-package
description: Use when the user asks to review, validate, or check readiness of an assembled requirements package; says 'review the requirements package', 'validate requirements', 'check requirements readiness', 'requirements review', 'check scope/completeness/consistency/measurability/testability', 'requirements handoff readiness', 'is the requirements package ready for the architect'. Independently invocable; assumes the package is already assembled.

name: analyze-repository
description: Use when the user points at a code repository and asks what kind of project it is, which reverse-engineering skill to apply, how to document it, or when they describe a monorepo / hybrid / multi-project codebase without specifying the type — including mainframe / COBOL / copybook / JCL repositories. The diagnostic step between having code and knowing which reverse-engineer-* skill to invoke.

name: reverse-engineer-api
description: Use when the user asks to document an API repository, reverse-engineer API docs, extract API documentation from source code, create OpenAPI specs from existing code, or build API consumer guides. Produces Part A (internal docs), Part B1 (OpenAPI spec), and Part B2 (consumer companion guide).

name: reverse-engineer-api-framework
description: Use when the user asks to document a backend / API framework, server-side library, middleware framework, or reusable backend components. Produces Part A (internal framework docs) and Part B (implementer docs for API developers using the framework). Do NOT use for individual API repositories — use reverse-engineer-api instead.

name: reverse-engineer-cobol-program
description: Use when the user asks to document COBOL programs, reverse-engineer COBOL source, extract documentation from a COBOL repository, document mainframe batch / online programs, document CICS / IMS / DB2 program logic, or build a program contract for COBOL callers. Produces Part A (internal docs for mainframe maintainers) and Part B (consumer guide for app integrators, batch schedulers, and downstream-system teams). Do NOT use for copybook-only repos — use reverse-engineer-copybook-library.

name: reverse-engineer-copybook-library
description: Use when the user asks to document a copybook library, reverse-engineer mainframe record layouts, build a coherent data dictionary across COBOL copybooks, normalize record layouts (REDEFINES / OCCURS DEPENDING ON), find duplicate or divergent copybooks across teams, or produce a per-copybook record reference. Produces Part A (internal docs for copybook maintainers and data architects) and Part B (data dictionary for application developers and integrators). Do NOT use for COBOL program repos — use reverse-engineer-cobol-program.

name: reverse-engineer-database
description: Use when the user asks to document a database (schema, stored procedures, triggers, views), reverse-engineer a schema, extract database docs, create a data dictionary, or generate ERDs from existing database code. Produces Part A (internal DB docs for DBAs), Part B1 (data dictionary & ERD), and Part B2 (database consumer guide for application developers).

name: reverse-engineer-jcl-job
description: Use when the user asks to document JCL job decks, mainframe batch jobs, PROCs / PROCLIB, INCLUDE members, IDCAMS / SORT / IEBGENER control cards, GDG dataset lifecycles, or scheduler integration on a mainframe. Produces Part A (internal docs for batch developers and ops) and Part B (job-flow guide for application teams and downstream consumers). Do NOT use for COBOL source — use reverse-engineer-cobol-program; do NOT use for copybooks — use reverse-engineer-copybook-library.

name: reverse-engineer-mobile-app
description: Use when the user asks to document a mobile application, Android app, iOS app, React Native app, or any mobile application repository. Produces Part A (internal app docs) and Part B (app overview & integration guide). Do NOT use for mobile frameworks/libraries — use reverse-engineer-mobile-framework instead.

name: reverse-engineer-mobile-framework
description: Use when the user asks to document a mobile framework or library, mobile SDK, Android AAR library, iOS pod / SPM package, or React Native npm module. Produces Part A (internal framework docs) and Part B (implementer docs for app developers). Do NOT use for mobile applications — use reverse-engineer-mobile-app instead.

name: reverse-engineer-test-suite
description: Use when the user asks to document a dedicated test-automation repository — E2E suite, integration suite, contract-test suite, BDD repo, or any standalone test project — regardless of stack (e.g., Cucumber/Java, Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, pytest, RestAssured, Karate, k6). Produces Part A (internal docs for test engineers maintaining the suite) and Part B (consumer docs for application developers and QE consumers calling the suite or relying on its components in the knowledge base). Do NOT use for application code with embedded tests — those are documented inside the application RE skill (`reverse-engineer-web-app` / `-mobile-app` / `-api`).

name: reverse-engineer-ui-framework
description: Use when the user asks to document a UI framework, component library, design system, or reusable UI components — for any underlying technology (e.g., React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid, Lit, Qwik, Web Components, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose). Produces Part A (full framework docs) and Part B (implementer docs for app developers using the library). Do NOT use for application repositories — use reverse-engineer-web-app instead.

name: reverse-engineer-web-app
description: Use when the user asks to document a web application, front-end app, SPA, MPA, or any user-facing web application repository — regardless of stack (e.g., React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid, Astro, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, Rails, Django, Laravel, ASP.NET MVC). Produces Part A (internal app docs) and Part B (app overview & integration guide). Do NOT use for frameworks/libraries — use reverse-engineer-ui-framework instead.
